question.text: In Cat I/II AIF waterfall terminology, the 'Preferred Return' is best defined as:

answer.text: The minimum guaranteed return to LPs contractually payable each year
The return generated in excess of the hurdle, split 80/20
The GP's share of first-loss protection
The return generated using the Hurdle Rate, which accrues entirely to investors before any GP carry

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 6: Preferred Return = return generated using the Hurdle Rate. It accrues ENTIRELY to investors on a pro-rata basis. It is NOT guaranteed (AIFs cannot offer assured returns); it is the threshold below which GP earns no carry. The Trap: A confuses 'preferred' with 'guaranteed' — SEBI prohibits assured returns in AIFs. C is nonsensical; D is the above-hurdle residual. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests same. SEBI AIF Regulation 10 prohibits guaranteed returns; preferred return is a waterfall construct, not a guarantee. Manager's Pro-Tip: In LP pitches, always say 'Preferred Return is a benchmark, not a guarantee'. A GP who implies guarantee attracts SEBI attention. Add PPM disclosure: 'Preferred Return is not assured; fund performance may fall below the hurdle.'
